note:
There's a class of game called 'hidden object' that's like 'where's waldo' but more interaction. One good example is 'hidden through time' (HTT 1 & 2). Price seems to be about $10 with 26 levels, ranging from 3-4 hidden objects for start/tutorial levels and 9-15 objects for bigger areas. The 26 are grouped into 4, with each group having around 6-7 levels. Average time looks to be in the 2m-6m range to solve.
It should be noted that the levels are dynamic and can be interacted (birds squak, trees shake, etc.). Sometimes the interactions are more fundamental, like revealing the inside of a house or tent with the potential for objects. For HTT, the items give a hover clue as to where to find it. Some other games are black and white and you can color them in with clicking.
WFC might be not well suited for much of the content as one of the draws is the unique interactions, items and scenes.
From the business side, doing a pilot of a 1-3 levels might be a way to gauge interest (release on itch.io, say). Shooting for 5min for the pilot, that's approximately 300 labor hours or about 2 months (full time).
Hidden folk units sold estimate is 0.5M. HTT1 is estimated at 80k units sold with HTT2 at around 10k units. I think Hidden Folk was one of the first breakthroughs of the genre and HTT is more recent.
